questions.q: Where does Overlook's appointment data actually originate, according to this lesson?
options: It is typed directly into OverlookDB by hand
A separate, existing third-party scheduling/booking platform that patients and front-desk staff use, which needs to feed into OverlookDB on an ongoing basis
It is generated automatically by the failover group
It comes from the Data Factory pipeline itself, with no outside source
questions.explain: The scheduling system is where new appointments are actually created first; OverlookDB needs an ongoing feed from it to stay useful.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe this ETL layer as Lesson 2's fifth piece rather than scope creep?
options: Because it was added on a whim
Because Lesson 2 explicitly planned five pieces for this capstone and named the ETL layer as the last one, dependent on everything before it
Because the board never actually asked for it
Because it has nothing to do with the rest of the capstone
questions.explain: This was planned from the start in Lesson 2's architecture, not bolted on afterward.

questions.q: Why does this lesson prefer Azure Data Factory over a manual export/import process?
options: Manual export/import is technically impossible for Azure SQL
A manual, person-dependent process is exactly what Lesson 1's mandate exists to eliminate — Data Factory moves data on a schedule without a person running it by hand
Data Factory is free while manual processes cost money
There is no real reason; both are equally good
questions.explain: The same reasoning that justified Chapter 5's automation applies to the data feed itself.

questions.q: Why is the Data Factory pipeline built last, in Chapter 6, rather than earlier in this capstone?
options: Data Factory cannot be configured until Chapter 6 technically
It needs somewhere stable, secured, and protected to write into — building it before infrastructure, security, or HA/DR existed would mean writing to nothing, or to an unsecured, unprotected target
There is no real reason, it's arbitrary
The board asked for it to be built last specifically
questions.explain: This matches Lesson 2's dependency chain: the pipeline depends on a stable, secured, protected target existing first.

questions.q: What would a perfectly secured, perfectly protected database that never receives new appointment data actually be, according to this lesson?
options: The ideal end state for Overlook
A museum piece — not solving a real problem for Overlook day to day
A failed deployment
Exactly what the board asked for in Lesson 1
questions.explain: The ETL layer is what makes the rest of this platform actually useful on an ongoing basis, not just secure in a vacuum.
